## Proposed use-case profile

Parsing, binding and useful review must be measured separately. A parser recognising a class is not enough to establish its inherited fields, canonical import identity or admissible review closure.

| Use case | Candidate treatment | Difficult boundary / required counterexample |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Plain annotated classes and local inheritance | Root plus exact field/base evidence; follow local bases and class-body aliases | Multiple inheritance, overriding fields, computed descriptors, metaclasses; don't imply flattened runtime model |
| Dataclass / attrs-like domain state | Recognise bound decorators, fields and local bases; start with stdlib/Pydantic dataclass patterns | Alias/shadowed decorator, init-only/class variables, slots and generated methods; attrs needs separate measured need |
| Pydantic BaseModel, RootModel, generics, custom model bases | Include model body, inherited local bases, validators, Field/Annotated metadata and config | Version-specific coercion, dynamic create_model, computed fields, validators in supporting code and arbitrary types |
| TypedDict and NamedTuple, class and functional forms | Extract explicit static field maps and required/optional markers, local inheritance | Computed field dictionaries, Required/NotRequired/ReadOnly/total, extra-items; don't execute factories |
| Type aliases / TypeAlias / type statements / NewType / enums / Protocol | Preserve nominal versus structural and generic distinctions | Plain assignment may be value alias; overloaded protocols and value-dependent expressions require omissions |
| Functions and async functions | Named top-level and methods with class context, parameters, return type, exact body and local references | Closures, class/staticmethod/property, overload groups, decorator factories, dispatch wrappers and mutable globals |
| Tool/node/router/validator decorators | Preserve exact decorated declaration; identify a bounded list through bindings, not spelling | Unknown wrapper may change identity/signature; decorator presence alone must not drop the whole function |
| Static import aliases and dotted references | Resolve lexical names and alias first segment; module import and member import differ | Shadowing, rebinding, conditional imports, same-named local/external packages |
| Relative imports / local absolute imports / package reexports | Define project import roots, package identity and transitive `__init__` reexports | Module-versus-package collisions, cycles, duplicate roots, implicit submodule lookup |
| src / flat / monorepo / local namespace layout | Use explicitly configured or unambiguous captured packaging metadata; multiple roots remain visible | `PYTHONPATH`, editable installs, custom backend discovery, namespace portions outside admitted root |
| TYPE_CHECKING / forward refs / future annotations | Resolve static annotation intent without evaluating it | Runtime/type namespace disagreement and unsupported annotation expressions |
| Stubs / third-party models | Support local `.pyi` evidence role and explicit framework/builtin boundary | A stub signature is not implementation evidence. No automatic environment scanning or cross-root source reads |
| wildcard / dynamic imports / runtime-generated schemas | Static literal `__all__` can be a bounded later feature; otherwise explicit omission | Exports can execute arbitrary code. Never import user modules for introspection |
| Untyped dictionaries / ORM Django / notebooks / C extensions | Include in measurement; initially visible limitations, then demand-led expansion | No declared domain shape, descriptors or generated/runtime source identities. Their omission counts against broad target |

Class root identity needs an explicit specification decision: whole-class exact source can include large method bodies and exceed existing evidence limits. A field-only model projection must not silently replace exact captured root source. Separate type-root projection, whole-class and method selection require accepted source/range contracts; supporting validators/bases remain required when a rule needs them. Budget omissions stay uncovered in the 90% metric.

This table is a proposal, not a claim that current Hapsland supports Python. Framework field metadata may be useful rule evidence; business-domain classification must come from examples and rule intent, not a framework name.

## How to establish the 90% target

The [shared language coverage plan](PRODUCT-RESEARCH-ADVISORY-2026-10-09-LANGUAGE-COVERAGE-PLAN.md#what-the-90-target-means) owns the canonical proposed endpoint, denominator and evaluation budget for both tracks. This section supplies Python-specific implementation detail and does not introduce a competing protocol. No result in this report establishes 90% coverage. Source files, declarations, import statements, edit events and useful reviewed roots have different denominators. The target should be decided before implementation as **at least 90% of independently labelled intended-user source edit/root cases successfully receiving admissible useful review evidence**. A valid omission is safe behavior but remains uncovered for this metric. Rule inapplicability, deleted roots, import-only edits, malformed input and capture exclusions need predeclared categories; report their rates rather than hiding them. Product-contract exclusions do not justify relabelling a broad user goal without stating the narrower denominator.

Proposed measurement steps:

1. Freeze a cohort of independent application repositories and actual agent edits, with AI app, AI backend/service and framework/infrastructure strata. Current six repositories are a discovery corpus; multiple related libraries are not six independent user populations. Limit dominant repositories and keep training/calibration repos separate from held-out projects.
2. Label edits/root units independently of the adapter: intended target(s), annotations/model family, imports/layout, required related code, correct canonical bindings, framework semantics relevant to the chosen rule, source/capture eligibility and expected omissions. An edit affecting multiple roots contributes all intended root cases plus event-level attribution success. Keep untyped and dynamic cases.
3. Freeze numerator: exact selected source/span, correct root identity, correct required binding closure or clearly sufficient root-only evidence, admissible rule input, and delivered review attempt under the accepted host contract. Record false bindings separately; a successful parse/provider call is insufficient. Review semantic accuracy needs separate human labels.
4. Report parse, extraction, attribution, binding closure, rule admission and delivery rates separately, plus end-to-end rate; show pooled, per-stratum and macro-per-project results. Every failure remains in the frozen denominator. No multiplying marginal rates as if stages were independent.
5. Follow the shared plan: 40 independent application repository clusters and 15 root opportunities per cluster, **600 held-out roots per language**, exercised with Add and realistic Update where meaningful. Report root and edit denominators separately. Keep framework/library discovery source separate from application-heavy holdout, with no shared lineage across development and holdout. Require observed useful-review availability >=90% per language and each included family, publishing equal-repository and opportunity-weighted estimates. The optional stronger gate is a one-sided 95% cluster-aware lower confidence bound >=90%, using a predeclared resampling protocol. Budget changes require a new declaration before observing held-out results. Run the frozen holdout once: failure or inconclusive results end that evaluation; later implementation iterations require a newly independent holdout. Do not tune on failed holdout cases and reuse the same sample as validation.
6. Replay changes and restoration for import metadata, aliases, reexports and dependencies. Run packaging/platform/native-host acceptance separately; exact source graph and useful rule evidence must be observed at the real provider boundary. Backend failure must preserve declared lifecycle behavior without changing the source coverage result.

The strongest case against a small Python adapter is that type annotations are common but binding and runtime model behavior span inheritance, decorators, descriptors and packaging conventions. These require a much broader profile than top-level functions/direct BaseModel classes. Current framework-heavy inventory may overestimate annotation demand and underestimate untyped notebooks/ORM/dynamic use cases. A simpler profile is acceptable only if held-out intended-user cases independently demonstrate the coverage target, not because a syntactic fixture passes.

## Resolution

Agreed with the owner across the Git-selection discussion:

1. With no explicit selectors, change mode selects all current uncommitted work: staged, unstaged, and untracked files. Normal file selection, exclusions, and protection policies apply. Explicit staged, unstaged, and untracked sources can narrow this selection.
2. A single non-merge commit selects changes introduced relative to its parent. A two-endpoint range selects the net difference between those states; intermediate changes undone by the endpoint are not selected. For the initial scope, a single merge-commit selector is unsupported: return an actionable error rather than infer a parent. Explicit endpoint comparisons remain available.
3. Support an explicit merge-base comparison against a user-specified branch/ref. Do not infer main, master, or upstream. This can be combined with uncommitted sources.
4. Combine sources as a union using a repeatable selector parameter. Do not introduce a separate comma-list grammar initially. Exact parameter names and invocation layout remain with the Effect CLI interface ticket. No explicit selectors means the agreed default; explicit selectors specify the union to use.
5. The output of selection is affected declarations without duplicates, not a blanket audit of every declaration in changed files. Review their current working-tree definitions and current permitted related context, including when selection originated from an index or historical diff.
6. Start with the simplest conservative mapping: review only declarations that can be associated unambiguously with current code. No heuristic recovery for renames, splits, or substantial rewrites is required. If mapping cannot be established, report a skip with its reason and mark the overall review incomplete. Do not fall back silently to a whole-file audit. Mapping internals remain an implementation choice; ambiguity must remain externally visible.
7. Deleted lines inside a surviving, unambiguously selected declaration select that current declaration. A fully deleted declaration or file has no current review target: record it as not applicable to current-code review. This alone does not make the review incomplete. Distinguish established deletion from inability to map a surviving or possibly surviving target.
8. Git sources provide candidates; includes, when configured or provided on the CLI, narrow candidates according to the resolved file-selection decision. Explicit CLI includes replace configured includes. Git mode does not require includes in addition to its explicit/default Git selection.

Examples: combining staged and unstaged changes affecting the same function reviews that current function once. Selecting an older commit that affected a still-identifiable function reviews its current body, not the historical body. An unresolvable historical-to-current target is skipped and makes the result incomplete; a confirmed deleted target is not applicable.

Exact selector names, invalid-input diagnostics, and the zero/partial-result exit codes are defined by the remaining CLI/result decision tickets. A root commit has no parent: implementation must handle that boundary explicitly or reject it with an actionable unsupported-selector error, never silently broaden selection.

This closes the product decision for Git selection. It authorizes specification work, not production implementation, historical-source review, or a claim of validated Git mapping behavior.

## Resolution

Agreed with the owner in the planning conversation:

### Output and progress

- Terminal progress consists only of file, declaration, and classifier-request counts. Do not list filenames or active filenames in progress. Distinguish request estimates from a known execution plan.
- In a terminal, update counters on stderr; emit findings and the final result on stdout. When output is redirected, use infrequent plain progress lines without animation.
- With --json, stdout contains one final JSON result, including partial results after interruption. Progress remains on stderr.
- Findings identify the file and declaration so users can act on them; the filename restriction applies to progress, not findings. Do not include source code in batch JSON by default.

### Errors and cancellation

- Continue independent work after a declaration-specific failure and report a partial result.
- Stop launching new requests on a run-wide failure, such as invalid configuration, invalid credentials, or backend-wide unavailability. Error classification must distinguish these from individual failures.
- Add no automatic batch-level retry loop. Preserve applicable existing provider behavior rather than silently promise zero retries at every layer.
- Ctrl+C stops new requests, attempts cancellation of active requests, and produces an honest partial summary. Requests already dispatched may still be processed by the provider. Existing provider/safety bounds remain; no new total-work cap is required.

### Freshness

- Reuse the existing direct-check freshness function per declaration before dispatch and after evaluation. The current single-declaration CLI already does this; resident advice-delivery authority is not the integration seam.
- Recheck retained results before the final batch report if this requires only a modest extraction of shared logic and retention of prepared inputs. Do not perform a substantial architectural rewrite solely for batch-final freshness.
- If final revalidation requires such a rewrite, retain per-declaration completion-time validation and explicitly identify that timing boundary in the result. Never imply the whole batch is an atomic current snapshot.
- Mark detected stale results as unavailable/currently invalid and make the overall review incomplete. Do not automatically restart their reviews.

### Completion status and exit semantics

- Complete review without findings: exit 0.
- Complete review with findings: a distinct nonzero exit code.
- Incomplete review, including errors, ambiguous mapping, or detected stale results: another nonzero exit code. Preserve any findings in the result; incompleteness takes precedence over findings for the exit status.
- Nothing to review (no selected files, eligible declarations, or applicable rules): nonzero with an explicit reason, not a clean-review claim.
- Ctrl+C: exit 130, with any completed partial result retained in output.
- Exact nonzero code allocation other than 130 remains with the Effect CLI interface decision. Existing single-declaration check semantics are not silently changed by this batch decision.

The result must make complete, incomplete, interrupted, and no-work outcomes distinguishable. Counters must remain meaningful under parallel execution; their exact field names and formatting belong to the CLI contract. This resolution is a product planning decision, not implementation or runtime-validation evidence.

### Commands and flags

Keep the capability in the existing rules command family:

- `hapsland rules audit`: review all eligible declarations in explicitly selected files. Explicit includes must come from configuration or the invocation; never infer a whole-repository audit.
- `hapsland rules check-changes`: review current declarations selected by the union of Git sources.
- Existing `hapsland rules check --path FILE --line N` remains the single-declaration entry, with its current semantics.

Both batch commands accept:

| Flag | Meaning and multiplicity |
| --- | --- |
| `--include PATTERN` | Repeatable nonempty repository-root-relative patterns. The union replaces configured root includes for this invocation. Omission inherits configured includes. |
| `--ignore-excludes` | Single boolean, default false. Disable ordinary global root exclusions only; preserve the accepted context-inheritance rule, explicit context exclusions, privacy protections, Git-ignore, and rule restrictions. |
| `--id ID` | Optional single enabled rule identity, reusing the existing check filter. Omission evaluates all eligible enabled rules. Unknown or disabled IDs are errors. |
| `--json` | Single boolean, default false. One final structured result on stdout, source excluded by default; counters on stderr. |

Only check-changes accepts repeatable Git source flags:

| Flag | Meaning |
| --- | --- |
| `--changes working` | All uncommitted work: staged, unstaged, and untracked. |
| `--changes staged` | HEAD-to-index changes. |
| `--changes unstaged` | Index-to-working-tree changes in tracked files. |
| `--changes untracked` | New untracked files, subject to normal selection/protection policies. |
| `--commit REF` | Changes introduced by a non-merge commit relative to its parent. |
| `--range FROM..TO` | Net difference between two explicit commit states. Require both endpoints; reject triple-dot and malformed/ambiguous ranges with an actionable message. |
| `--merge-base REF` | Difference from the common ancestor of REF and HEAD to HEAD. This selects committed branch work; add working explicitly to include uncommitted work. |

Union all explicitly provided sources. Apply default working only when none of these four Git flag groups is present. Repeated or overlapping sources never duplicate review declarations. No comma-list grammar or guessed branch names. Resolve references once for the invocation so moving branch names do not change the chosen endpoints midway.

Examples:

```sh
hapsland rules audit --include 'src/**/*.ts'
hapsland rules audit --include 'src/**' --include 'examples/**' --ignore-excludes
hapsland rules check-changes
hapsland rules check-changes --changes staged --changes unstaged
hapsland rules check-changes --merge-base main --changes working
hapsland rules check-changes --commit abc123 --range def456..abc123 --include 'src/**' --json
```

Audit rejects Git flags. Both batch commands reject single-declaration path/line and mutation scope flags. Unknown flags, missing/empty values, invalid selectors, and invalid singleton repetition fail before provider requests. Valid include repetitions form a union. Empty configured include selection cannot broaden scope. Commands must explain that Git sources select current-code targets, not historical reviews. Unsupported merge/root-commit selectors and unresolvable references produce actionable diagnostics, not inferred comparisons.

### Exit-code allocation

- 0: complete, no findings.
- 1: complete, findings present.
- 6: incomplete or unavailable, including detected stale results. This matches the existing application mapping for incomplete; retain findings in the report.
- 7: no work, with distinct reasons for no selected files, no eligible declarations, and no applicable rules.
- 130: interrupted, preserving completed partial results.

Invalid invocation/configuration uses the existing CLI failure path (currently 6). Machine consumers distinguish invocation failure without a batch report from an incomplete batch report by the presence and status of the structured result. Do not route the batch through a generic partial status that would accidentally select the application's unrelated code 5. Existing single-declaration exit codes remain unchanged.

### Effect CLI and documentation ownership

Use Effect CLI declarations and the actual parser, not hand-parsed argv or a second executable grammar. Retain domain ownership in the rules capability and selection policy in its existing owner; no new top-level command framework or workspace package is justified.

Extend the existing generated rule reference to include all batch flags, type/choices, requiredness, repeatability, defaults, examples, exit statuses, and valid/invalid combinations. Prefer supported structured Effect help output when it exposes the needed facts. Do not couple generation to Effect APIs marked internal. ## Resolution — observed candidate validation and focused task checks

The operator authorized “review with astra then if all good accept.” An independent `gpt-6.2-astra` review returned **ACCEPT, no blockers**, satisfying that conditional acceptance. ### Minimum useful validation before activation

Reuse Traits’ saved-rule/task-file review and repair loop, adapting it to Hapsland’s supported declaration evidence and the already accepted requirement to observe candidate behavior before activation. `check_rules` evaluates the exact unsaved candidate through the existing review preparation/evaluation owners while active rules remain untouched. The candidate must match the intended effective compiled rule, settings, threshold and permitted policy/evidence; bypassing selection or privacy to make a test run is not validation.

The agent first independently inspects the example and states the expected finding/clear judgment and why. Select the smallest relevant example set that actually exercises the intended concern. A clear-only result does not establish violation sensitivity. Add a discriminating boundary or nonfinding example when applicability, exceptions or an overly broad question warrant it; no mandatory synthetic positive/negative pair, fixture format or calibration program is required. Prefer relevant real task declarations. Do not alter production code merely to fabricate validation fixtures.

Show expected versus actual observed judgments, the selected declaration, permitted supporting evidence and omissions, effective rule identity, probability, configured threshold and resulting finding/clear decision. A finding on a known violation example is successful candidate validation. It is distinct from a confirmed source finding in task code that requires triage and repair. Structural/schema validity alone is not evidence of useful behavior; evaluated/exit 0 does not mean finding-free.

For example, a rule requiring admitted inputs to return an explicitly declared result rather than throw or return outside the signature should find a visible `head(xs: number[]): number` implementation that throws for an empty array. A version explicitly returning `number | undefined` can be an expected clear case only if that is the intended remedy; a requirement for an always-numeric result would differ. These are proposed expectations illustrating the method, **not observed classifier results**. Neither result would prove general totality or termination. A requirement that every API change update repository documentation cannot be enforced through declaration review and must be explained as unsupported rather than saved with a false enforcement claim.

A relevant expected/observed mismatch blocks activation. Repair or revise and revalidate, reject, or defer. Missing required context for a supported declaration is an explained skip, distinct from an unsupported preference at admission. Skipped, unavailable, stale, failed or inconclusive checks are incomplete, never clear. Report the actual reason and obtain appropriate supported context or authorization where needed; do not invent a confidence cutoff or treat absence of a request/result as success. Changed candidate content needs renewed validation and the exact final content/actions still need approval under the accepted conversation/application contracts.

### Focused checks after application and coexistence with advice

After approved application, inspect the actual saved/active state and check eligible declarations changed or directly involved in the task using the affected saved rules. Distinguish saved, activated and checked outcomes. Inspect findings in context, repair confirmed source violations with minimal behavior-preserving changes, and recheck changed inputs. Ask where behavior changes, scope or authorization require operator judgment. Never weaken a rule just to silence a source finding. On operation failure inspect actual state before retrying; use ordinary repair/rejection or return to an observed working state. No inactive-candidate store or automatic rollback subsystem is mandated.

Group related edits into bounded verification checkpoints. Automatic advice continues to consume existing rules only; it never initiates introduction/refinement. Reuse an existing candidate or automatic observation only when the exact effective rule, model/request settings, selected source, supporting evidence and any accompanying rules that affect the request are unchanged and equivalence can actually be established. Otherwise perform a fresh bounded check. This is an optional optimization, not a requirement to build a reuse subsystem. Do not claim a subset, stale observation or an empty selection proves current task compliance.

### Scope, privacy, cost and truthful reporting

Use explicit eligible task paths/lines inside the working tree and supported declarations with bounded related code. Preserve current privacy/exclusion, evidence, credential and resource/provider boundaries. No whole-repository audit, new Git selectors, glob interface, credential exposure or automatic source-bearing evidence retention is authorized. Keep source-bearing input/output private.

Explain the configured remote backend, selected scope and possible charges; report actual classifier request counts and meaningful omissions. Stay within existing bounded project cost/authorization policy. This decision is not blanket consent for paid runs. Use a small bounded set, avoid unchanged failing retries, and obtain authorization when expanding beyond existing authority. Current provider-limit uncertainty remains uncertainty; do not claim byte checks prove token budgets or account cost limits.

Report the scope and snapshot actually evaluated, expected/observed outcomes, unresolved findings, skips, failures and decisions needed. Observed examples establish those cases, not general classifier accuracy, formal correctness, repository-wide compliance or runtime support.

Inspected installed Traits **0.5.16** and the D&D reference `.agents/skills/traits/SKILL.md`: saved-name checks of task files, exact unchanged review reuse, explicit eligible-file scope, contextual triage, repair/recheck and truthful incomplete outcomes are reference practices.
